legend: A grasshopper starts at position 0%%ZSMJ0%% on a number line containing the points 0,1,2,…,n%%ZSMJ1%%.

Each minute, the grasshopper chooses a point j∈{0,1,…,n}%%ZSMJ2%% that it has not chosen before and jumps over it. If the grasshopper is currently at position i%%ZSMJ3%% and jumps over point j%%ZSMJ4%%, it lands at position 2j−i%%ZSMJ5%%.
After exactly n+1%%ZSMJ6%% minutes, the grasshopper has jumped over every point 0,1,…,n%%ZSMJ7%% exactly once. It is guaranteed that after all jumps, the grasshopper returns to position 0%%ZSMJ8%%.
Your task is to count how many permutations of the jump-over points result in this behavior.
input: The first line contains an integer t%%ZSMJ9%% — the number of test cases.
Each of the next t%%ZSMJ10%% lines contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ11%% (2≤n≤75)%%ZSMJ12%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all values of n%%ZSMJ13%% over all test cases does not exceed 75%%ZSMJ14%%.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the number of valid orders of jump-over points modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ15%%.
note: Each point from 0%%ZSMJ16%% to n%%ZSMJ17%% must be jumped over exactly once.
The order of jump-over points matters.
Some values of n%%ZSMJ18%% may have zero valid permutations.
Since the answer can be large, all results are taken modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ19%%.
For example, when n=4%%ZSMJ20%%, one valid order is: [ 0, 1, 2, 4, 3 ] After performing these jumps, the grasshopper returns to position 0%%ZSMJ21%%.
